dataset.title: Studies of metabolosome type bacterial microcompartment core enzyme interaction networks and their potential applications as antimicrobial targets, mass spectrometry data

dmp.description:
Bacterial microcompartments are prokaryotic organelles consisting of a quasi-icosahedral
or polyhedral protein shell and an encapsulated enzymatic core. The encapsulated enzymatic cores perform
concerted functions, such as carbon fixation in the case of carboxysomes, and the catabolism of various
substrates like ethanolamine, propanediol, glycerol, choline, rhamnose, fucose, and others in the case of
metabolosomes. While the core enzyme interaction networks are well-known for carboxysomes,
metabolosomes are much less studied in this regard. While short, often amphipathic sequences designated as
encapsulation peptides (EPs) have been demonstrated to be responsible for enzymatic core-shell interactions,
their role in core-core interactions remains largely unknown. We propose to systematically and comparatively
investigate the EP-mediated interactions of six different types of BMCs, identify the interaction partners, and
visualize these interactions using structural biology methods. Since one of the main functions of
metabolosomes is thought to involve the containment of toxic aldehyde intermediates, we will also explore the
possibility of using identified EPs to disrupt the formation of the enzymatic core, thus providing a proof of
concept for their usefulness as antimicrobial targets.
